I much prefer physics where I can see practical applications, or philosophy where we explore ideas rather than crunch numbers. Math feels like a necessary evil in my education.

If zero, one solution. If negative, complex solutions. Honestly, I always double-check my work because I'm prone to calculation errors.

From what I remember in physics class, stationary points are where the function isn't changing - like peaks, valleys, or flat spots. First, find the derivative f'(x).
